text:
Nina (People Ops): FYI — one quick question from Diego who traveled to Berlin last week: he used a mix of cash and card for meals. Some small cafe receipts are missing because the till printed faded receipts. What's the policy for missing international receipts + per diem?

Diego (Sales): yeah sorry. Had a couple €5-10 coffees with no readable receipt. I kept a photo of the cup and the card payment for the taxi but not for the cafes. Can I claim per diem instead of itemized?

Sam (Finance): short answer: for international day trips under 24 hours you can choose per diem or actuals. If you pick per diem, you don't need individual meal receipts. If you pick actuals, we need receipts for any single line item over €25 (or equivalent). Small missing receipts under €25 can be approved with a short attestation.

Diego (Sales): ok what's the attestation look like?

Sam (Finance): copy/paste this into the "Missing Receipt Explanation": ```I, Diego, attest that the following small purchases occurred on 2026-02-14 in Berlin (total €13.50): single-serve coffees and a bakery purchase. Receipts were illegible/expired. Card/taxi receipts and hotel folio attached.``` We'll also need the per-day currency and totals.

Rory (IC): if I choose per diem, is it the US rate or local rate in euros? Also do we cover VAT or exchange fees? :question:

Sam (Finance): per diem uses the local country per diem table (see travel policy). It covers meals + incidental expenses; VAT is included in the per diem implicitly so don't submit VAT-only claims when using per diem. If you paid in a foreign currency and have receipts, enter amounts in the original currency; our expense tool will auto-convert using the bank rate on transaction date. Bank fees for foreign ATM withdrawals are reimbursable as a separate line item (attach fee statement).

ExpenseBot: Note — default Germany (DE) per diem: 60 EUR/day (meals & incidental). Partial-day rules: travel starts/ends before 0600 or after 2000 qualifies for full-day. See /travel-per-diem for details.

Nina (People Ops): what about tipping? some countries have different norms — do we reimburse standard tips?

Sam (Finance): reasonable tips are reimbursable. For Germany, rounding to 5-10% for cafes/restaurants is typical; attach receipt or include in attestation for cash tips without receipt. No receipts required for per diem.

Diego (Sales): hotel incidentals (mini-bar) — if I used per diem do I still claim them separately?

Sam (Finance): incidental charges that are not meals (e.g., business calls, conference printing) can be claimed separately even if you used per diem. Mini-bar snacks are considered meals/incidentals so roll them into per diem unless a single item is > €25 and you have a receipt and can claim actuals.

Rory (IC): edge case: I bought snacks for a team working late and want to code to "team-retention" expense. Is that allowed under travel?

Sam (Finance): if the purchase was during travel and for a client/meeting, use the appropriate cost-center and put a short justification. If it's internal team food, use the team events policy — not travel. We'll route accordingly.

Diego (Sales): last piece — can I submit the monthly bank statement as backup for small cash spending?

Sam (Finance): bank statement is helpful but not sufficient for cash transactions. The attestation plus any supporting docs (hotel folio, card txns, photos) will suffice for items under the threshold. Anything > €25 needs a receipt.

Nina (People Ops): perfect. I'll add the attestation snippet and DE per diem numbers to the travel FAQ. Diego — we'll approve this once you attach the attestation and hotel folio. :white_check_mark:
